races_in_feed: statewide (Governor/Lt. Governor, Secretary of the State, Treasurer, Comptroller, Attorney General), Congress, State Senate and House, judges of probate, registrars of voters, questions
local: no (Connecticut has no county government; towns report into CTEMS)
how_counted: Each town reports its own count as it finishes.
count_order: No ballot-type split; results by town with each town's status.
vote_types: no split by ballot type seen; results are by town, with each town's status '( Official Results )' and precincts reported

certify.rule: Votes for members of Congress are counted on the last Wednesday of November (Conn. Gen. Stat. 9-315); state officers are declared by the General Assembly on the first day of its session (9-318); the Legislature's results are declared in November (9-319).
certify.local_rule: Towns report within 48 hours of the polls closing (Conn. Gen. Stat. 9-314).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

rehearsal: 80 (Nov 2022 state election, the same offices as 2026), 111 and 112 (Aug 11, 2026 primaries), and the posted 108, kept in election_cache/replay/sources/<code>-<id>/ (kept 2026-10-10 by N10 for rehearsals)
scout_blocked: nothing refused scripts (Cloudflare front, no challenge)
scout_plan: Live-readable. Poll election/108/Version.json every two to three minutes; when the number changes, fetch stateVotes, townVotes and townStatus for that version (Lookupdata once, keeping only names and parties). Town figures give the map below the state. Rehearse on election 91 (2024) in October. Probate and registrar races come from the same files, so Connecticut's local level is covered the same night.
notes: Lookupdata carries an address field 'AD': never read it.

Reader (N10, 2026-10-10): pcc_ems. check() reads election/<id>/Version.json; fetch() the version's five files. Lookupdata's address and contact fields are never read. A candidate on several party lines is one person, the lines added.
